WITH race_totals AS (
  SELECT
    r.raceId,
    c.country,
    SUM(cr.points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM races AS r
  JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
  JOIN constructorResults AS cr ON cr.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country
),
average_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(entry_count) AS avg_entry_count
  FROM race_totals
)
SELECT
  rt.raceId,
  rt.country,
  rt.total_points,
  rt.entry_count,
  rt.entry_count - ac.avg_entry_count AS above_average
FROM race_totals AS rt
CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac
WHERE rt.entry_count > ac.avg_entry_count
ORDER BY above_average DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The average entry count is across races with at least one constructorResults record; races with no entries have no count to aggregate and are excluded.

alternatives.interpretation: Include races with no constructor result entries as zero when calculating the average across all races.
alternatives.sql:
WITH race_totals AS (
  SELECT
    r.raceId,
    c.country,
    SUM(cr.points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(cr.constructorResultsId) AS entry_count
  FROM races AS r
  JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
  LEFT JOIN constructorResults AS cr ON cr.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country
)
SELECT
  raceId,
  country,
  total_points,
  entry_count,
  entry_count - (SELECT AVG(entry_count) FROM race_totals) AS above_average
FROM race_totals
WHERE entry_count > (SELECT AVG(entry_count) FROM race_totals)
ORDER BY above_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
